meta.title: Case study: hosting and cybersecurity for an entrepreneur self-assessment
meta.description: How Axenor took a third-party app to production, secured it and ran it: cloud migration, custom domain, least privilege, backups and an orderly shutdown.

hero.title: Self-assessment for entrepreneurs
hero.lead: We did not build it. We took it to production, secured it and ran it.
hero.text: An entrepreneurship organization had a founder test built by a third party, running on a prototyping platform, with a QR code already printed and in circulation. We took over hosting and security: we migrated it to a cloud we manage, closed the gaps and kept it stable until the campaign ended.

challenge.title: The challenge
challenge.text: The app worked and the QR code was already printed, but it ran on an environment meant for prototypes: no backups, no deletion protection, database permissions wider than needed and more connections than the database could handle at peak.

solution.title: What we did
solution.text: We migrated the app to a cloud we manage, redirected the existing QR without breaking links or campaign analytics, set up a custom domain with an automatic certificate, left the database on least privilege with automatic backups, and tuned capacity for event peaks.

result.title: The result
result.text: The whole campaign ran on the new infrastructure at roughly 28 USD a month. When it ended we delivered a verified backup of everything and shut the resources down so the client stopped paying.

architecture.title: Before and after
architecture.subtitle: Same app, same QR code. What changed was everything holding it up.

qr.title: Printed QR code in circulation
qr.text: It pointed straight at the prototyping platform.

host.title: Prototyping platform
host.text: Hosting and database on third-party accounts, with no direct control.

capacity.title: Untuned capacity
capacity.text: Up to 50 connections against a database that accepts about 25.

qr.title: The same QR, redirected
qr.text: Permanent redirect that keeps links and campaign parameters.

run.title: Container on Cloud Run
run.text: No servers to maintain, 4 instances max and 160 concurrent sessions.

db.title: PostgreSQL 17 on Cloud SQL
checks: Role that can only read and insert
30 retained backups plus a verified one
Deletion protection and a disk cap

guards.title: Guards around it
guards.text: Credentials in Secret Manager and a budget with alerts at 50, 90 and 100%.

security.title: Cybersecurity in practice
security.subtitle: Concrete controls for an app with personal data and event traffic.

privilege.title: Least privilege
privilege.text: The app connects with a role that can only read and insert. It cannot delete or change existing data.

secrets.title: Secrets out of the code
secrets.text: Credentials live in Secret Manager and environment files are excluded from the repository and the images.

backups.title: Backups and deletion protection
backups.text: Automatic backups with 30 retained, a verified manual backup and deletion protection on the instance.

inherited.title: Review of what we inherited
inherited.text: We audited permissions, costs and failures in the previous setup, and verified every finding before acting.

transport.title: Encrypted traffic, own domain
transport.text: HTTPS with a managed, auto-renewing certificate, with the campaign served from a domain under our control.

spend.title: Brakes on abuse and spend
spend.text: An instance cap and a budget with alerts: a traffic spike or an attack does not turn into a surprise bill.

reliability.title: Stable through event peaks

connections.label: database connections, tuned to what it can actually handle

cost.label: a month to run, 93% of it the database

scale.label: assessments a month possible with no extra compute cost

reliability.fixes: While taking it to production we found and fixed two issues affecting operations: a connection leak that could take the service down, and a double submit that left users stuck right after answering all 28 questions.

closure.title: A shutdown as careful as the launch
closure.text: When the campaign ended we did not just switch it off. We delivered a complete, verified package so the client can restore the service whenever they want, on this cloud or another, and then shut the resources down.
